explanation: Chinese writers described sailors steering by magnetized needles in the early 1100s, decades before the first European record. Shen Kuo had already described the needle compass in 1088.

claims.text: Magnetic compasses were first used for navigation at sea in China.
Records of compass navigation in Europe, Portugal and Scandinavia included, are later than the Chinese records, and the ancient Greeks had no magnetic compass.
Chinese texts of the early 12th century describe sailors navigating with magnetized needles.
The earliest European record of a magnetic compass, by Alexander Neckam, dates from about 1190.
Shen Kuo described a magnetic needle compass in 1088.
